title: What If You Flew to the Center of the Milky Way?

scenes.text: What if you flew to the center of the Milky Way? Something waits there that you can't see.
It's about 26,000 light-years away. Light leaving it today needs 26,000 years to reach us.
At the center sits Sagittarius A star, a black hole about four million times the mass of the Sun.
You couldn't see the hole itself, only the glowing gas around it. The first image came in May 2022.
A star called S2 circles it every sixteen years, passing at almost three percent of the speed of light.
Yet a traveler wouldn't be pulled in by default. Objects can orbit it safely, like Earth orbits the Sun.

description:
What if you flew to the center of the Milky Way?
A black hole four million times the Sun's mass is waiting, but you could orbit it safely from a distance.
